title: Brazilian License Plate Validator
description: Check locally whether a Brazilian plate matches the Mercosul/PIV or old format, with conversion notes and no official lookup.
metaDescription: Check locally whether a Brazilian plate matches the Mercosul/PIV or old format, with conversion notes and no official lookup.

details.title: What this validation covers
details.description: The tool separates format, character conversion, and scope limits.

formats.title: Two Brazilian patterns
formats.description: Mercosul/PIV uses LLLNLNN, such as ABC1D23. The old PNU format uses LLLNNNN, such as ABC-1234.

conversion.title: A-J table
conversion.description: When converting from the old pattern to PIV, the second digit becomes a letter from A to J.

noLookup.title: No official lookup
noLookup.description: Does not query public or private databases and does not confirm vehicle data.

privacy.title: Safe link by default
privacy.description: The plate enters the link only if the explicit share-content option is checked.

officialLookup.question: Does this validator query SENATRAN, DETRAN, or RENAVAM?
officialLookup.answer: No. It runs in the browser and validates only the plate format and character-conversion table.

existence.question: Does a valid plate mean the vehicle exists?
existence.answer: No. A valid format does not confirm existence, ownership, registration, fines, restrictions, authenticity, QR Code, or cloning.

format.question: What is the Brazilian Mercosul plate format?
format.answer: The Brazilian PIV/Mercosul pattern uses seven characters in the LLLNLNN sequence, such as ABC1D23.

conversion.question: How do I convert an old plate to Mercosul?
conversion.answer: Keep the three letters, the first digit, and the last two digits. Replace the second digit with A-J: 0 becomes A, 1 becomes B, 2 becomes C, through 9 becoming J.

oldEquivalent.question: Why do some Mercosul plates have no old equivalent?
oldEquivalent.answer: Reverse conversion through the old table exists only when the fifth position is A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, or J.

privacy.question: Is the typed plate saved or sent to the server?
privacy.answer: Not by this tool. Validation happens in the browser and there are no favorites, API, official lookup, or plate storage.

sharing.question: Can I share a link with the plate filled in?
sharing.answer: Yes, only after checking the option to include the plate in the link. Do that only when anyone with the URL may see that data.

seo.about: The plate validator checks in the browser whether a Brazilian plate follows the current PIV/Mercosul pattern or the old PNU pattern. It also shows equivalence through the A-J table used for character conversion.
seo.howToUseTitle: How to validate a Brazilian plate online
seo.howToUse: Type or paste a plate, check the status, and copy the normalized version, formatted display, or conversion when available. The tool does not query SENATRAN, DETRAN, RENAVAM, QR Code, or any official database; include the plate in a link only when it may be visible to whoever receives the URL.
